source_observations: NextToken emits integer tokens for decimal and 0x-prefixed values; decimal tokenization accepts an optional leading minus, while hexadecimal scanning accepts only ASCII hex digits.
The 0x branch constructs an INT token even when readHexNumber returns an empty string, so the lexically accepted token literal is 0x; this is not a numeric-range or parser-acceptance guarantee.

The lexer does not enforce a 16-bit operand range. The exact pinned lexer also tokenizes 0, 0x10000, -1, and 65536 as INT values; downstream parser/emitter/assembler behavior remains a separate contract.
Operators relevant to conditional expressions include ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=, &&, and ||. Source positions track byte and UTF-8 character offsets separately.
Whole-file reading also covers comment skipping, identifiers, strings, raw strings, Unicode decoding, and end-of-input handling; no claim is made that these paths are fully validated.
